overview: URLs are produced to Kafka keyed by host so one consumer handles a host at a time and rate-limits locally; content hashes dedupe pages.

estimation.result: Network, object storage and host politeness dominate the design.
estimation.implication: Shard frontier ownership by host; global worker parallelism must never violate a single host's delay budget.

components.purpose: Identify due work and dispatch bounded batches for web crawler.
components.rationale: Persist schedule/progress and fence partition or leader ownership so failover does not create uncontrolled duplicate dispatch.

components.purpose: Partition URLs by normalized host. A consumer owns host pacing, robots.txt rules and crawl-delay; pause the partition instead of hammering a hot host.
components.rationale: Ordering is within a partition; checkpoint only after durable effects and dedup replays.

components.purpose: Execute background work with bounded concurrency for web crawler.
components.rationale: Assume retries; identify work stably, fence obsolete attempts and commit results before acknowledgement.

components.purpose: Resolve a name or select a nearby regional entry for web crawler.
components.rationale: DNS caching and TTL affect failover speed; do not rely on instant propagation.

components.purpose: Bloom filter in front + content fingerprint dedup
components.rationale: Define the partition key and consistency requirements; conditional writes protect version and ownership checks.

components.purpose: Persist immutable large objects for web crawler.
components.rationale: Publish metadata pointers only after objects are complete; use checksums, versioned keys and lifecycle cleanup.

accessPatterns: Check/claim a URL; update status and content fingerprint after fetch.
constraints: A Bloom filter is only a probabilistic accelerator; confirm positives when false-positive omissions are unacceptable.

accessPatterns: Write compressed content; downstream processors read by object key.
constraints: Enforce size limits, supported schemes, robots policy and safe redirect handling before fetching.

apiDetails.purpose: Internal administrative contract for seeding or scheduling a crawl.
apiDetails.rationale: This system does not require a public consumer REST API. Normalize/dedup URLs and enforce per-host politeness before dispatch.

apiDetails.purpose: Worker task contract for one bounded fetch.
apiDetails.rationale: Acknowledge only after content and URL state commit; retry with the same task identity.

steps.title: Re-crawl scheduler → Host-partitioned URL log → Fetchers
steps.explanation: Partition by normalized host; one owner enforces robots.txt and crawl delay. Pause a hot host instead of flooding it.

steps.title: Fetchers → Seen URLs
steps.explanation: Check durable URL/content deduplication with a bounded task lease.

steps.title: Fetchers → Raw pages
steps.explanation: Store fetched content before committing consumer progress.

steps.title: Fetchers → Host-partitioned URL log
steps.explanation: Publish discovered links using stable URL identity.

steps.title: Re-crawl scheduler → Host-partitioned URL log → Fetchers
steps.explanation: A new consumer resumes offsets and restores per-host pacing state; duplicate downloads are deduped.

failureCases.scenario: A fetcher dies after downloading but before acknowledging
failureCases.handling: Redeliver the leased task; dedup by normalized URL/content hash. Preserve per-host next-allowed-fetch time across ownership changes and back off repeatedly failing hosts.

alternatives: Use priority/front/back host queues for fine scheduling and fairness. Use a host-partitioned log for replayable ownership, handling hot hosts, partition pauses and pacing state across rebalances.
